Definition: from G1537 and G4098; to drop away; specially, be driven out of one's course; figuratively, to lose, become inefficient:--be cast, fail, fall (away, off), take none effect.
BiblicalUsage: Scripture uses ekpíptō where we would say to fall away, to fail. In Acts 12:7, the text says "Arise up quickly. And his chains fell off from [his] hands." In Romans 9:6, the text says "Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they [are] not all Israel."
TheologicalSignificance: Reading ekpíptō this way, I believe falling away is real, and the warning is given so that we hold fast instead. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
